outliers.recommended_angle: Christian's version will mirror the structure by highlighting the fragility of building on rented platforms like social media. He'll contrast the panic of an algorithm change with the stability his FieldWork members have by owning their own automated systems, reframing AI from a content toy to an infrastructure tool.
my_hooks: How long until you own the engine of your business?
When the algorithm changes again, will you be scrambling?
What if your business didn't depend on social media?
Your entire business is built on rented land.
Stop letting an algorithm decide your income.
my_talking_points: How long until it’s all built in house?
I have a few founders in my FieldWork program who have already built their own automated client systems using simple AI tools.
And watching everyone panic last month when the algorithm changed again, seeing their reach get cut in half overnight, it really made me think.
How long until most experts figure out you can build a client and content engine that you own completely, one that works for you 24/7 without being dependent on a single platform?
Now, it takes some initial work to set it up, and I don't think most people have the focus to build these foundational assets yet.
But the folks inside FieldWork are sleeping well at night. They aren't scrambling because they own the system that brings them clients.
You have to realize that AI is not just for writing your social media posts or summarizing notes.
AI is for building the core infrastructure of your business, the engines that allow you to own all the pieces.
It’s for building systems that make your work more effective and less manual, so you can buy back your time.
If building a business that runs itself so you can get back to your life sounds interesting, comment the word 'FIELDWORK' below and I'll send you a guide on how we do it.
